reason: I'm not putting an unaudited startup with zero customers in the execution path of every agent trade on my venue, and the identity check rests on a passport registry the vendor's own founder started. My team can build caps, a human-approval queue, a kill switch and a hash-chained log inside a quarter, and then I can explain every line of it to my examiner.
objection: The trust anchor is AINRA, and it's their own registry. If my last exam asked how we use AI, I can't answer 'a pre-revenue vendor's in-house standard decides which agents can trade', and I can't vouch for a proxy sitting inline on order flow with no SOC 2.
would_change_my_mind: A finished SOC 2 Type II plus support for an identity standard the vendor doesn't control, so their registry isn't the only gate, and a couple of regulated venues already running it in production.
